  - [1mBenchmarks / Leaderboard (model & prompt-version comparison)[0m — CLAUDE.md calls this a headline capability ("identifies how different model/prompt versions impact performance"). Completely undocumented and genuinely hard to self-discover.
  - [1mThe in-product AI assistant ("Agent")[0m — ironic gap: the feature that [3manswers[0m these doc questions has no page describing what it can do. Users literally ask an assistant "what can you do?".

  [1mMedium[0m
  - [1mLatency / Performance[0m — perf analysis pages, undocumented.
  - [1mLabels / AI labeling[0m — powers custom-chart [38;5;153mgroup by label[39m, product areas, labeling rules; referenced obliquely but never explained.
  - [1mNotifications & scheduled reports[0m (Slack digests, daily TL;DR) — I linked the per-chart digest to [38;5;153mintegrations/slack[39m, but the broader reporting system has no home.
  - [1mInsights / Recommendations / Brainstorm[0m — the AI-guidance surfaces.

  [1mProbably intentional / low priority[0m
  - [1mFindings[0m — deliberately folded into Issues (there are [38;5;153mplatform/findings → platform[39m redirects), so a section in [38;5;153missues.md[39m beats a new page.
  - [1mTraces, Events (reading), Session Review[0m — thinner; likely fine as subsections.
  - Admin/settings pages (Members, Plan, Audit Logs, Blocklist, Webhooks) — real gaps but lower question-volume than the analytics pages.

  My recommendation: [1mOverview[0m and [1mUsers & organizations[0m are the two I'd do first — they're the biggest holes, and the latter closes a loop the docs I just wrote open.

  Want me to draft any of these? I'd suggest starting with those two (same house style, same corpus), or I can do the whole "highest value" tier.
